title: Ah Whither Should I Go
description: Ah Whither Should I Go in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 152. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ah whith-er should I go, Bur-dened, and sick, and faint? To whom should I my trou-bles_ show, And pour out my com-plaint? My Sa-viour bids me come, Ah! why do I de-lay? He calls the wea-ry sin-ner home, And yet from him I stay!

lines: To whom should I my troubles show,
He calls the weary sinner home,
And yet from him I stay!
What is it keeps me back,
Which will not let my Saviour take,
Some idol, which I will not own,
Which I have feared to see:
Yet let me now consent to know
What keeps me out of thee:
According to my faith to me
O let it, Lord, be done!
In me is all the bar,
Remove it, and I shall declare

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
